title: Site selection engine: p50/p95 latency fusion with path-resilience scoring
creator: Marisol Vega
description: Implement an improved site (region/POP) selection engine that fuses p50 and p95 latency telemetry with a compact path-resilience / network-health score to drive tier-aware routing and model-variant fallbacks. The goal is deterministic, low-latency choices under normal load while enabling graceful degradation when network signals indicate instability.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic ranking function produces the same top-3 candidate sites for 95% of stable telemetry windows between experiments
Routing policy respects tier constraints (hosted / dedicated / private) and prefers same-tier sites unless network-health delta > 20 points
Fallback matrix triggers model-variant downgrade (e.g., fp16 -> int8) automatically when chosen site's p95 crosses configured hysteresis for 3 consecutive windows
System exposes metrics: chosen_site_latency_p50, chosen_site_latency_p95, chosen_site_nethealth_score, fallback_trigger_count
End-to-end integration tested with synthetic network jitter and packet-loss scenarios in staging (scripts + dashboards linked)
steps: Design scoring function doc in Confluence and get PM/design alignment
Implement telemetry ingestion aggregator to compute windowed p50/p95 and path metrics (packet loss, RTT variance, retransmit rate)
Build network-health scalar (0..100) combining loss, jitter, and recent route flaps using EWMA smoothing
Create ranking service that fuses normalized p50/p95 with nethealth and tier penalty to produce a ranked site list
Add fallback policy engine mapping site health to model-variant and region-tier fallbacks
End-to-end test automation and rollout as a staged feature flag with canary to 5% of traffic
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff with PM (Ravi Patel) and SRE; agreed on target metrics and data sources (edge telemetry, pop-heartbeats, envoy stats)
2026-02-20: Confluence spec v0.1 created: /confluence/redwood/smart-routing/site-selection-fusion (see doc) — linked code sketch for ranking formula
2026-02-27: Telemetry aggregator prototype finished; emits p50/p95 windows and packet_loss_percent per POP (PR: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pulls/412)
2026-03-04: Net-health scalar prototype validated against last 30 days of historical incidents; EWMA half-life tuned to 10 minutes to reduce flapping
2026-03-08: Ranking service skeleton implemented; deterministic normalization (z-score) added for p50/p95 pre-fusion (PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pulls/87)
2026-03-10: Integration test added for fallback path: artificially increase p95 and packet loss to trigger variant downgrade; failed (race condition in feature-flag check) — debugging underway
decisions: Use both p50 and p95 in fusion: p50 influences primary ordering during stable conditions; p95 acts as a risk penalty for tail latency bursts
Normalize p50/p95 to z-scores per-site using a rolling 24h baseline to account for geographic differences
Network-health score is a 0..100 value composed of: 40% packet_loss_score, 30% jitter_score, 20% retransmit_rate_score, 10% recent_route_change_score
Apply asymmetric hysteresis: require 3 consecutive windows above threshold to trigger a fallback, and 5 consecutive windows below threshold to restore
Tier penalty: cross-tier routing allowed only when preferred-tier sites have nethealth_score < preferred_site_score - 20 (guardrail to avoid gratuitous cross-tier moves)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overreacting to transient spikes may cause unnecessary fallbacks -> Mitigation: EWMA smoothing + consecutive-window gating
Risk: Normalization amplifies noise for low-traffic POPs -> Mitigation: Minimum-sample threshold and fall back to absolute thresholds when samples < 50
Risk: Cross-tier routing could violate enterprise constraints -> Mitigation: Respect explicit tenant routing policy and include header-based override for Dedicated/Private
Risk: Telemetry lag introduces stale decisions -> Mitigation: Prefer short-window p50 for freshness and mark nethealth with freshness metadata; increase sampling frequency for critical routes
manual_test_plan: Run synthetic jitter test: apply 50ms of jitter to eu-west-1 for 15 minutes and verify that chosen_site_nethealth_score drops > 25 and fallback is invoked
Packet loss spike: drop 2% packets for 10 minutes and assert no single-window flip; requires 3 consecutive windows to downgrade variant
Failover verification: simulate regional blackout in staging and ensure routing chooses next best site within 1s of policy decision
notes: Next: fix race in feature-flag gating, add per-tenant override rules, and schedule a 2-hour runbook review with SREs before canary rollout. PM asked for a dashboard widget showing top-3 candidate sites and contributing signals (p50, p95, nethealth) per decision.
